findings.title: findMany() removed without updating any callers
findings.body: This PR removes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method from InsightsBookingService and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. The service no longer exposes any method that actually executes a query — consumers must now call `getBaseConditions()` and embed the result in their own `$queryRaw` (as the new test does). However, the PR only touches this service file and its test file; no consumer (e.g., the insights tRPC router or wherever this service is used to list bookings) is updated. If any existing caller still invokes `service.findMany(...)`, the TypeScript build will fail; if callers were expected to migrate, that migration is missing from this PR. Verify all consumers of InsightsBookingService are updated or confirm none exist before merging.

findings.title: Org/team scope authorization SQL is never executed against the database
findings.body: The tests for org-scope (line 332-343) and team-scope (line 295-299) authorization conditions only assert structural equality of the generated `Prisma.Sql` object; they never run the SQL. The only test that actually executes a query via `$queryRaw` (the `getBaseConditions` test) uses user scope, which contains only `"userId" = $1 AND "teamId" IS NULL`. As a result, the `= ANY(${array})` parameterization and the `isTeamBooking` column reference used exclusively in org/team scope are never validated — a wrong column name, bad array binding, or syntax error there would only surface at runtime in production, in the authorization-critical path. Previously the object-notation conditions were type-checked by Prisma (`BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`); raw SQL strings get no such checking, so execution coverage matters more. Compounding this, the PR description states the author could not run the tests at all. Add an integration test that executes the org-scope and team-scope conditions against the real database.

findings.title: Org-scope assertion depends on row order of an unordered DB query
findings.body: The org-scope test asserts the generated SQL equals `... "userId" = ANY(${[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]}) ...`, i.e. it requires the user IDs to appear in exactly that order inside the `Prisma.Sql` values array. That order comes from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which applies no `ORDER BY`, so Postgres is free to return membership rows in any order (e.g., after index changes or table growth). Any reordering makes `toEqual` fail even though the generated SQL is semantically identical, making this test flaky. Either sort the IDs before asserting, or compare the values order-insensitively (e.g., sort the `values` array before comparison).

findings.title: Caching behavior tests removed while caching logic remains in the service
findings.body: This PR deletes the entire 'Caching' describe block (the two tests verifying that repeated calls to `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached results), but the caching implementation (`cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` fields and the `undefined` check in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`) is still present in the service. If the caching is intentional, its regression coverage is lost; if it is no longer needed, the fields and checks should be removed instead. Note the caching uses `undefined` as the sentinel while `cachedFilterConditions` can be `null`, so the distinction matters and is worth keeping under test.

findings.title: PR description misrepresents the change as test-only
findings.body: The PR description states: 'This PR updates the InsightsBookingService integration tests to work with the new Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation.' In fact, the diff converts the service implementation itself in this PR (replacing `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` with `Prisma.sql`, removing `findMany`, adding `getBaseConditions`, changing the constructor's options type, and reworking `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`). Reviewers relying on the description may skip reviewing the service change, which is the higher-risk part (raw SQL in an authorization path). The description should be corrected to state that this PR performs the service conversion plus the test update.
